_comment: CAD text styles are named after the font file AutoCAD used, and almost every
drawing names a font this build is not allowed to redistribute: the .shx set is
Autodesk's, and the TTF names (simsun, arial, ...) are Microsoft's.
So instead of shipping those fonts, every name a drawing is likely to ask for is
mapped onto one of two open fonts and served under its original name. The viewer
resolves a style name through this catalog, finds a real file, and never raises
the 'missing font' notice. The glyphs are Noto's, not the original's, so a
single-stroke SHX face becomes a sans-serif one - text is legible and complete,
just not a pixel-identical copy of the plotted sheet.
Names are matched case-insensitively by the viewer; they are written here as
they appear in drawings. The Chinese font also carries the Latin, Cyrillic and
kana glyphs, so an ambiguous name belongs to it rather than to the Latin one.
Hangul is not covered. A drawing that uses it still reports a missing font and
needs -cad-fonts-dir with a Korean face in it.
